# heytownhall_api_key (Resource)

A data API key. Destroying the resource revokes the key.

The API shows a key's secret once, when the key is created. The provider keeps it in the Terraform state in `secret` (marked sensitive) because nothing can read it again. Anyone who can read the state can read the secret, so keep the state in an encrypted backend with restricted access. A key that is imported has no known secret, and `secret` stays null.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "heytownhall_api_key" "staging" {
  name = "staging"
  kind = "sandbox"
}

# The secret is known only because Terraform created the key. It is kept in the state.
output "staging_key" {
  value     = heytownhall_api_key.staging.secret
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `kind` (String) `sandbox` (fictional towns, free) or `live` (real data, billed). Changing it replaces the key: the old key is revoked and a new one with a new secret is made. A live key needs live billing to be open on the organisation.
- `name` (String) A name to tell the key apart, such as `production` or `staging`. Changing it renames the key.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the key was created (RFC 3339).
- `display` (String) The key's prefix and last four characters, as the dashboard shows it.
- `id` (String) The key's id.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The full key, for example `htd_live_...`. Known only when Terraform created the key; null for an imported key. Stored in the state.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the key's id. The secret stays null: the API shows it only once, when the key is created.
terraform import heytownhall_api_key.staging 3f0c1c1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
```
